old_also.hook: ~60 stalls: 9 fish, 11 butchers/charcuterie, fruit & veg, plus the outer ring of pagès farm stalls · esmorzar de forquilla territory by 9am
old_also.text: The working municipal market, in a 1944 hall of ~1,712 m². Mon–Fri 07:00–14:00, Sat to 14:30, closed Sun. A locals' market — go early, the fish counters thin out by mid-morning.

old.name: Fesols de Santa Pau (DOP)
old.text: Small beans of the Tavella Brisa, Setsetmanera and Gra Petit varieties, grown only on the volcanic soils of Santa Pau and six Garrotxa villages — EU-protected (Reg. 2015/1312). The reason a plate of botifarra amb seques tastes of the Garrotxa and not just of beans.

old.name: Poma de Girona (IGP)
old.text: Five varieties (Golden, Gala, Granny Smith, Fuji among them) grown on the Gironès–Empordà plain, PGI-protected since 2003 (Reg. 1491/2003). The Ter's water and cold nights give a firm, high-acid apple — the everyday fruit of the province.

old.text: A grey-moulded goat's cheese from the Garrotxa, matured at least 21 days — EU-registered as a PGI only in December 2023 (Reg. 2023/2872), so recent. Nutty, faintly mushroomy from the rind; the backbone of any Girona cheese board.

old.name: DO Empordà cellars
old.text: The Alt/Baix Empordà DO, founded 1975, ~1,768 ha of low bush vines held down by the tramuntana. Visit Espelt (Vilajuïga), La Vinyeta (Mollet de Peralada), Masia Serra (Cantallops) or Terra Remota (Sant Climent Sescebes) — most take booked tastings.

old.name: Oli de l'Empordà
old.hook: A PDO oil pressed mainly from the local Argudell olive — the plain's other liquid.
old.text: Protected as a PDO by EU Implementing Regulation 2015/385. The zone covers the Alt and Baix Empordà with parts of the Pla de l'Estany and the Gironès; the oil is at least 51% Argudell, with Curivell, Llei de Cadaqués and Arbequina alongside. Green, faintly bitter, cut for pa amb tomàquet and for finishing suquet.

old.name: Passeig de la Muralla
old.hook: The wall-top walk on a Carolingian circuit over Roman foundations.
old.text: One of the longest early-medieval wall circuits in Europe, 9th–10th c., rebuilt over 1st-c. BCE Roman lines because Girona sat on the Carolingian–al-Andalus frontier. Free; open 8:00–21:00 (to 23:00 Jun–Aug). The towers give the best rooftop views of the Cathedral and the plain.

old_also.name: Passeig de la Muralla
old_also.hook: The wall-top circuit — the city's high edge.
old_also.text: A walkable rampart on one of Europe's longest Carolingian wall circuits (9th–10th c.), laid over Roman fortifications because Girona guarded the frontier. Free, open dawn to night; the towers are the best free viewpoint over the Cathedral, the Barri Vell roofs and the plain of the Ter.

old.name: The Cathedral-to-Sant Feliu spine
old.hook: The stone heart, from the widest nave to the eight Roman tombs.
old.text: From the Cathedral's Baroque staircase down Pujada de Sant Domènec to the Basílica de Sant Feliu, where eight 3rd–4th-c. Roman and early-Christian sarcophagi are set into the presbytery walls — the densest run of history in the city, walkable before breakfast.

old.name: The Call labyrinth
old.hook: The steep black-stone lanes of the medieval Jewish quarter.
old.text: Off Carrer de la Força, the Call folds into stepped alleys, cisterns and dead-ends — one of Europe's best-preserved Jewish quarters. End at the Museu d'Història dels Jueus in the Centre Bonastruc ça Porta. Wear grippy soles; the stone polishes to glass in the rain.

old.name: The Onyar bridges
old.hook: Seven bridges, one row of reflected houses.
old.text: Walk bank to bank across the Onyar's footbridges — the Eiffel-company Pont de les Peixateries Velles (1877) is the one to stand on — watching the cases de l'Onyar double themselves in the water. The colours were fixed by a 1980s restoration led by the painter Enric Ansesa and architects, not chosen at random.

old_also.name: Cases de l'Onyar & the Eiffel bridge
old_also.hook: The reflected houses and the iron bridge that frames them.
old_also.text: The ochre-to-rust river façades are the city's signature; their palette was fixed by a 1980s restoration led by the painter Enric Ansesa. The Pont de les Peixateries Velles that crosses between them was built in 1877 by Gustave Eiffel's company — two years before he built Girona nothing else, and two decades before Paris got its tower. The personal-design credit is disputed; the firm and the year are documented.

old.name: Parc de la Devesa
old.hook: The largest urban park in Catalonia, under 2,500 plane trees.
old.text: On the Mercadal side, a grid of plane trees planted in the 19th century throws deep shade over gravel avenues; it doubles as the fairground for the Fires de Sant Narcís each autumn. Bring a book and disappear.

old_also.name: Parc de la Devesa benches
old_also.text: Under the tallest plane trees in Catalonia the temperature drops several degrees; the gravel avenues are where locals sit out the worst of the afternoon heat.

old.name: Vall de Sant Daniel
old.hook: A green valley of springs and plane trees ten minutes past the walls.
old.text: Behind Montjuïc the city stops and a wooded valley of natural springs (the Font del Ferro among them) runs up to the Romanesque monastery of Sant Daniel. A cool, shaded escape in August and the quiet counterweight to the Barri Vell.

old.name: Castell de Sant Miquel
old.hook: A hill climb to the ruined castle above the city, for the whole valley.
chips: Early, for the haze to lift
old.text: A signed path leaves the Vall de Sant Daniel and climbs through holm oak to the ruined Castell de Sant Miquel (~380 m), with the four-river plain, the Pyrenees to the north and, on a clear day, a glint of the Costa Brava. Take water.
